tickets.title: Sellers can set a reserve price
tickets.description: When listing an item a seller can set an optional reserve price, at least the starting price. If the auction closes with a highest bid below the reserve, the item is unsold and no winner is announced. Bidders see whether the reserve is met, never its amount.

steps: P1: Add a new requirement 'Reserve price': optional reserve when listing, must be at least the starting price (else rejected); auction ending with highest bid below reserve is unsold with no winner; bidders see only whether the reserve is met, never its amount. Add acceptance criteria for each rule.
P1: Amend REQ-001 to mention the optional reserve price, and REQ-004 so the highest bidder wins only if the reserve (when set) is met, otherwise the item is unsold.

P2: Item (DSN-015) gets reservePrice (number | null) and a reserveMet() method; ItemView (DSN-017) gets a reserveMet flag (boolean | null) and must not carry the reserve amount; list views of open items must also hide it.
P2: ItemController.listItem and ItemService.listItem take an optional reservePrice and validate it against the starting price; update UC-002 and SEQ-002.
P2: ItemService.closeDueAuctions marks the item unsold with no winner when the reserve is not met; update UC-005 and SEQ-005. ItemStore (DSN-029) persists the reserve column.

P2: BidEventPublisher and AuctionEventPublisher payloads carry reserveMet, never the reserve amount; WebClient (DSN-042) shows a reserve field in the listing form and 'reserve met / not met' on the item page; reflect in UC-003.

P4: Implement the changes in Item, ItemView, ItemController, ItemService, ItemStore (schema column), both publishers, the routes in app.ts (strip the reserve amount from GET /api/items and GET /api/items/:id) and public/index.html.

P5: Add tests: reserve below starting price rejected; listing without reserve still works; close below reserve gives unsold without winner; close at or above reserve gives winner; item views and live events expose reserveMet but no reserve amount; ItemStore round-trips the reserve.

report.text:
TCK-001 asked for an optional reserve price on listings. The reserve must be at least the starting price. An auction that closes below the reserve ends unsold with no winner, and bidders only ever see whether the reserve is met, never the amount.

Requirements (P1): REQ-012 "Reserve price" is new. Its criteria cover rejecting a reserve below the starting price, the close rules, showing reserve met or not met on item pages and lists, never exposing the amount, and carrying the reserve-met state in live bid and close events. REQ-001 now lists the reserve as an optional field. REQ-004 now says the highest bidder wins only when there is no reserve or the reserve is met, and that watchers see the unsold state when there is no winner. Changing or removing a reserve after listing was added to out of scope. The phase recorded three assumptions that still need confirming:
- the reserve is entered and stored in the item currency
- whether sellers can see their own reserve amount (not covered now; nobody can see it after listing)
- items without a reserve show no reserve indicator at all

Design (P2): Item (DSN-015) gets a reservePrice attribute and two new methods, isReserveMet() and close(). There is a new PublicItem interface (DSN-044) for data sent to clients. It has a reserveMet field and no reserve amount. ItemView, ItemController and ItemService now return PublicItem, and listItem takes a reservePrice parameter. The list item, place bid and close auction scenarios (SEQ-002, SEQ-003, SEQ-005) now show the reserve parameter, the isReserveMet call and the close call. The publishers, ItemStore, LiveGateway, the components and UC-002 to UC-006 now also trace to REQ-012. One criterion was left without a design mapping: REQ-008's "no admin role". A reviewer should decide whether the design as a whole covers it.

Code (P4):
- Item checks the reserve and now holds the close logic that used to sit in ItemService.closeDueAuctions.
- ItemService rejects a reserve below the starting price and converts items to PublicItem before returning them.
- ItemStore persists the reserve. On older databases it adds the missing column at startup.
- Both event publishers add reserveMet to their payloads.
- The HTTP route passes reservePrice through, defaulting to null.
- The web client has an optional reserve field and shows "reserve met" or "reserve not met" when an item has a reserve.
- The README tables were updated to match.

The test phase (P5) updated six test files for the new constructor and listItem signatures. Typecheck failures after P4 came from tests still using the old Item and listItem signatures, not from the code. P5 also added tests for REQ-001 AC4 and AC5, the reordered REQ-004 criteria (now AC2 to AC6) and REQ-012 AC1 to AC8. Final result: 57 passed, 0 failed. The earlier P5 summary also mentioned 8 todo tests.

Still open:
- The UC-004 test for the live reserve-met state checks for a reserveMet field in the bid event. The design does not define the event payload, so this name was taken from PublicItem. It matches the code, but the payload shape is still not in the design.
- Check that the renumbered REQ-004 criteria and the updated SEQ-002, SEQ-005 and SEQ-006 scenario tests match what the requirements mean.
- No test exercises the client-side reserve display in public/index.html.

steps.summary: The agent read and then wrote the requirements for TCK-001, adding REQ-012 for an optional reserve price, updating REQ-001 and REQ-004, and adding changing or removing a reserve after listing to out of scope. Both tool calls succeeded, and the final reply flags that the document has no UC-, SEQ- or DSN- items, so the P2 design steps have nothing to map to and will need updating in their own phase. Before approving, check the three open questions on REQ-012 (currency, whether sellers can see their own reserve, and what bidders see when there is no reserve) and confirm that leaving post-listing reserve changes out of scope is what you want.

The design phase P2 now covers the reserve price and close rules, and the design saved with coverage recorded after one failed report_coverage call that was retried successfully. The one uncovered criterion, REQ-008 AC6 ("no admin role"), is a design-level property rather than a method, so the reviewer should decide whether it can be accepted as covered by the design or needs another mapping. Check the assumption that reserves are entered and stored in the item currency, and note that sellers cannot see their own reserve amount because PublicItem hides it from everyone.

The agent regenerated the code for phase P4 to the new design, and drift and the app start check both pass, but typecheck still fails in four test files under `test/` (DSN-029, UC-003, UC-004, UC-005) because they call the old `Item` and `ItemService.listItem` signatures and need a `reservePrice` argument added, which the agent says it can't edit. Before approving, check whether someone else owns those tests so the fix can happen, and confirm that the new `close()` behaviour (highest bidder wins, otherwise unsold, with reserve checks) matches what the design requires.

The agent patched the tests for the new reserve-price behaviour, and typecheck is clean with 57 tests passing and 8 todo, so no code bugs were reported. Before approving, check the reserve-met event test in UC-004, because it looks for a `reserveMet` field that the agent guessed from the public item shape since the design does not define the payload. Also confirm the retitled REQ-004 criteria (AC5 and AC6) and the changed SEQ-002, SEQ-005 and SEQ-006 scenarios match what the requirements actually say.

+functional, must
+
+The system shall let a seller set an optional reserve price when listing an item, reject a reserve below the starting price, and show bidders only whether the reserve is met, never its amount.
+
+Acceptance criteria:
+
+- A listing with a reserve price lower than the starting price is rejected with an error message and no item is created.
+- A listing with a reserve price equal to or higher than the starting price is accepted.
+- A listing without a reserve price is accepted and works as before.
+- When the auction closes with a highest bid below the reserve, the item is unsold and no winner is announced.
+- When the auction closes with a highest bid at or above the reserve, the highest bidder wins.
+- Item pages and lists of open items show whether the reserve is met (reserve met / not met) for items that have a reserve.
+- No item view, item list, API response or live event sent to bidders contains the reserve amount.
+- Live bid and close events carry the reserve-met state, so watchers see it update without reloading.
+
+## Assumptions
+
+- Assumed: Is the reserve price entered and stored in the item currency, like the starting price and bids?
+- Assumed: Should the seller be able to see their own reserve amount after listing (e.g. on their item page)? The ticket says only that bidders never see it.
+- Assumed: For items without a reserve, should the item page show no reserve indicator at all (assumed), or something like 'no reserve'?
+
 ## Out of scope
 
 - Payment processing
 - Notifications to winners or other users (the winner only sees the result on the item page)
 - Passwords, accounts with login and an admin role
 - Scale beyond demo level (more than 200 watchers per item or more than a few bids per second)
 - Display currencies other than CHF, EUR and USD
+- Changing or removing a reserve price after the item is listed
